content:
- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 10–15 days).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early and overshoot after sharp price spikes in history.
- Model exhibits strong mean reversion bias — overestimates after recent high prices, underestimates after recent lows.
- Forecast horizon 30d shows persistent lag: true prices often dip below forecast mid-cycle, then recover — model fails to anticipate downward correction.
- Model underestimates prices in late cycle (last 5–10 days of 30d window), especially when true prices show upward momentum.
- Overshoots after spikes in history (e.g., 72+ → forecast 75+), then fails to correct downward — model doesn’t adjust for post-spike volatility.
- Model is sensitive to recent history: if last 5 days are high, forecast tends to stay high; if last 5 are low, forecast stays low — lacks dynamic adjustment.
- Forecast tends to be smoother than true price, missing short-term volatility spikes and troughs.
- Model underestimates prices when true price is trending upward — especially in late 30d window.
- Model overestimates when true price is trending downward — especially in early 30d window.
